I am an old woman of 69 years, farming this small piece of land that my family owns. For my yam and cassava, I use what I have always used — the cuttings and tubers I save from last season, and the droppings from my few animals around the compound. Fertilizer from the shop is costly and not something we put on cassava and yam here; I save my small money for food and medicine. My children and grandchildren help me with the heavy work like making the ridges, but my hands are not as strong as before, so I will pay one or two young people to help me clear and mound the soil.
